standard.title: Fasteners — Threaded Steel Fasteners — Step Bolts for Steel Structures — Specification (First Revision)
standard.sector: Production and General Engineering / Bolts, Nuts and Fasteners Accessories

standard.description: This standard specifies the material, mechanical, dimensional, manufacture, and test requirements for step bolts used in steel structures, including electrical transmission towers, to gain physical access to the top of the structures.
standard.scope: This standard specifies the material, mechanical, dimensional, manufacture, and test requirements for step bolts used in steel structures, including electrical transmission towers, to gain physical access to the top of the structures.

certification.description: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Bolts, Nuts and Fasteners (Quality Control) Order' issued by the Government of India, all step bolts utilized on structural steel masts and transmission towers must conform to IS 10238 and bear the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Manufacturing, importing, or selling uncertified step bolts in the Indian market is a statutory offense. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to heavy industrial steel fasteners.
requirements: Every step bolt package or batch must carry the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the manufacturer's registered licence number (CM/L).

For climbing safety reasons, the maximum total weight of a person—including their personal climbing tools, nuts, tackles, and gear—using these step bolts to ascend must not exceed 150 kg (or 120 kg in early standard drafts).
Each individual step bolt must be packaged and supplied complete with exactly two matching hexagon nuts.
The step bolt must belong to Product Grade C as specified in IS 1367 (Part 2), and satisfy property class 4.6 as specified in IS 1367 (Part 3).
The hexagon nuts supplied with the step bolts must belong to property class 5 and comply with IS 14394.
The accompanying plain washers must be Type A punched washers conforming to IS 2016, but feature a modified heavy-duty thickness of 5 ± 1 mm.

The step bolt must feature M16-6g screw threads complying with IS 4218. The thread pitch must be P = 2 mm, with a 2x45° end chamfer, and all edges must be smooth with zero sharp corners to prevent worker injury.
Permissible surface discontinuities of the step bolts must comply with the strict quality limits of IS 1367 (Part 9/Sec 2).

The finished step bolts must be hot-dip galvanized in accordance with IS 1367 (Part 13), and the washers galvanized per IS 4759. All dimensional limits specified in the standard apply to the product before galvanizing is executed.

Immediately after galvanizing, the hot-dip galvanized bolts, nuts, and washers must be passivated by dipping in a 0.15 percent solution of sodium dichromate with 0.5 percent concentrated sulphuric acid maintained at a temperature above 32°C to prevent wet storage strain (white rust).

To verify climbing safety, the step bolt must be tightly fixed to a structural member via a 16 mm drilled hole with the nuts tightened to the end of the threads, as illustrated in Fig. 2. The assembly must be subjected to a cantilever proof load of 150 kg (specified as 120 kg in some earlier prints) applied for 10 seconds. After unloading and re-applying the load for another 10 seconds, there must be no permanent set observed at the designated measurement point, subject to a measurement error tolerance of 30 µm.
Sampling, inspection, and acceptance criteria must conform to the standard procedures of IS 1367 (Part 17).
The step bolts must be designated by size, length, standard number, and the suffix 'NN' indicating two nuts (e.g., 'Step Bolt M16 x 175 NN IS 10238').
Each step bolt must carry the manufacturer's identification mark and the property class (4.6) marked on the bolt head in accordance with IS 1367 (Part 3).
